name: Vespa
model: Typed documents with text, fields and tensors; text, vector and structured search with ML ranking run on the content nodes
engine_note: Custom C++ content nodes: in-memory attribute fields and posting lists plus disk-backed document store, transaction log, HNSW for vectors
consistency: Single-document atomic, with conditional (test-and-set) writes; no multi-document transactions. Writes synced to disk before ack. Replicas are eventually consistent; after a successful write, search sees it by default.
scaling: Horizontal and automatic: documents go into buckets placed by a CRUSH-like algorithm; adding or removing nodes moves a minimal set of buckets. Queries fan out to all content nodes.
version_note: Vespa ships many 8.x releases per week; any recent 8.x is current. Spun out of Yahoo as Vespa.ai on 2023-10-03 (https://blog.vespa.ai/vespa-is-becoming-its-own-company/).
reach: Reach for it when search or recommendation ranking needs ML models (tensors, multi-phase ranking) over large, frequently updated data at low latency.
avoid: Avoid for a small app with simple keyword search; its configuration model (application packages, schemas) is heavy to learn and run.
escape: Postgres cannot rank millions of documents with ML models per query at low latency.
chat: Ranking for semantic search over all messages, combining text match, embeddings and recency in one query.
notes: Consistency quotes: 'Vespa offers configurable data redundancy with eventual consistency across replicas.'; 'Multi-document transactions are not supported.'; 'Writes are guaranteed to be synced to durable storage prior to sending a successful response to the client'; 'After a successful response, changes to the search indexes are immediately visible by default.' Elasticity quote: 'The ideal state distribution algorithm uses a variant of the CRUSH algorithm to decide bucket placement'. Engine note summarised from general Vespa docs (attributes, document store), not fetched page by page. No Jepsen analysis.
